September 29, 2026

Jack Smith tells Congress evidence showed Trump committed serious crimes

tags: politics, legal
sources: @aaronparnas

Former special counsel Jack Smith testified under oath before Congress that his investigation developed proof beyond a reasonable doubt that President Trump engaged in serious crimes against the nation, and said he would bring the same charges again regardless of the defendant's party. Smith said Trump engaged in a criminal scheme to overturn the 2020 election and prevent the lawful transfer of power, and that after leaving office he illegally retained classified documents at Mar-a-Lago and repeatedly obstructed efforts to recover them. During the hearing, Missouri Republican Senator Eric Schmitt accused Smith of attending an Atlanta Hawks game with Fani Willis; Smith said the game was a University of Iowa Hawkeyes match against Maryland that he attended with a Marshals Service detail. Schmitt stood by his line of questioning and left the hearing room.

Civil rights groups sue to keep ICE agents away from polling places

tags: politics, legal
sources: @aaronparnas

A coalition including the NAACP and Protect Democracy has filed a lawsuit seeking to bar immigration agents from being deployed at polling places, with under 40 days remaining before Election Day. The suit argues that Section 11(b) of the Voting Rights Act prohibits not only turning voters away but also threatening or intimidating them at the polls. Advocates say armed agents at polling sites would deter turnout in Black, Latino and Asian immigrant communities where residents face a higher risk of being racially profiled.

Migrant children as young as two appear in Texas immigration court without lawyers

tags: immigration, legal
sources: @aaronparnas

CNN reported on a Texas immigration courtroom where unaccompanied migrant children, some as young as two, appeared before a judge without legal representation. Among those who appeared was a 13-year-old Honduran boy who told the judge his mother and nearly his entire family were in the United States and that returning to Honduras was too dangerous; the judge said he did not qualify for asylum and asked whether he wanted voluntary departure or a removal order. The boy was given until the end of the month to appeal the deportation order.

Taxpayer-funded Trump ad draws bipartisan criticism ahead of midterms

tags: politics, media
sources: @groundnews, @total.hypocrisy

The Trump administration is spending public money on a 30-second television advertisement adapted from Trump's 2024 campaign, which closes with the line "Paid for by the U.S. Government." AdImpact said spending on the spot has exceeded $319,000. The ad shows Trump describing a "final battle" against the deep state, globalists, warmongers, communists and the news media, and is part of a series of government-funded spots featuring the president before the midterm elections. Lawmakers from both parties have criticised the ads; the White House calls them public service announcements, comparing them with past campaigns that promoted Medicare and COVID-19 vaccination rather than a sitting president.

Lawsuit challenges Medicaid work requirements for medically frail adults

tags: health, politics, legal
sources: @aaronparnas

The administration is seeking to implement a rule under the One Big Beautiful Bill Act requiring adults who receive Medicaid through the Affordable Care Act expansion, covering 40 states and Washington, D.C., to document a set number of work hours or other qualifying activities to obtain or keep coverage. The only exemption requires a person to establish that they are medically frail and that their condition significantly impairs their ability to meet the requirement. Democracy Forward has filed suit, Taylor et al. v. Kennedy et al., against the Secretary of Health and Human Services to block the rule, which is not yet final.

Education Department rescinds Title IX protections for LGBTQ students

tags: politics, legal
sources: @aaronparnas

The Department of Education has formally rescinded a Biden-era rule that extended Title IX sex discrimination protections to students on the basis of sexual orientation and gender identity. The rule had been challenged in court. Advocates say the rollback weakens protections for sexual assault victims and for transgender athletes. The administration says it will issue its own interpretation of the rule.

Proposed rule would fast-track Arctic drilling approvals on 23 million acres

tags: climate, politics
sources: @carolinegleich

The Bureau of Land Management is advancing a rulemaking, sought by the oil and gas industry, that would streamline environmental review for oil and gas development across 23 million acres of public land in Alaska's Western Arctic. Rather than assessing each project's effects on wildlife, Indigenous communities and the ecosystem, the rule could approve projects on the scale of the Willow development in as little as 60 days, bypassing current review and public input requirements. Indigenous families in the region have hunted caribou and fished the area's rivers for generations. A public comment period is open until November 9.

UK police arrest five near air base used for US strikes on Iran

tags: legal, defence
sources: @groundnews

British police are holding five men on suspicion of preparing a terrorist act following arrests near RAF Fairford, an air base used by the United States. The Metropolitan Police said the men were initially detained on suspicion of offences under the Explosives Act. Gloucestershire police declared a major incident and army bomb disposal specialists examined several vehicles, with nearby households evacuated. RAF Fairford has supported US strikes on Iranian missile sites during the US-Israeli war with Iran; a US Air Force spokesperson declined to discuss force protection measures.

Swiss voters reject tighter neutrality rules

tags: politics, defence
sources: @groundnews

Swiss voters rejected a constitutional initiative to tighten the country's neutrality rules, with 70.15% voting no and 29.85% voting yes on provisional official results. Turnout was 47.06% and the measure failed in every canton, missing the double majority required for constitutional amendments. The proposal would have barred Switzerland from joining or cooperating with military alliances unless attacked, and from imposing sanctions on countries at war without United Nations approval. The right-wing Swiss People's Party backed the measure after Switzerland sanctioned Russia over its invasion of Ukraine, while the government said it would weaken national security and block training with NATO.

Federal funding decision halted pediatric brain cancer clinical trials

tags: health, politics
sources: @aaronparnas

CNBC reported that the National Cancer Institute notified the Pediatric Brain Tumor Consortium in August 2025 that it would not be able to reapply for federal funding, blocking new patient enrolment in several trials. At least two clinical trials for children's brain cancer treatment were shut down, and the start of other trials was delayed by about a year. Four additional trials were transferred to larger hospital networks, producing a 13-month gap during which no patients could enrol.

New York prosecutors reopen Cornell fraternity rape case

tags: legal
sources: @groundnews, @aaronparnas

Tompkins County District Attorney Matthew Van Houten said a criminal inquiry will be reopened into a woman's allegation that she was drugged and raped by multiple men at Cornell University's Chi Phi fraternity house in October 2024, and that the case will go before a grand jury. The woman, identified as Jane Doe, alleges seven men assaulted her after she became intoxicated and used ketamine, leaving her unable to consent; Van Houten said her 2024 police statement had described the drug use and sexual conduct as voluntary. Cornell disputed claims that it failed to punish those involved, saying sanctions included expulsions and suspensions, and an attorney for one man named in the civil lawsuit denied his client took part in any sexual activity. TMZ reported that one of the men has lost his job at a Wells Fargo branch in Charlotte, North Carolina, in a decision tied to the district attorney's announcement.

Paxton defends plea deal that cut child sex abuse charge to a misdemeanour

tags: legal, politics
sources: @aaronparnas

Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton was confronted over a plea agreement his office offered a man charged with child sex abuse that called for a single day in jail. Paxton responded that the man served 60 days, saying it was not the outcome his office wanted and that it did not control the sentence. The plea deal reduced a felony charge to a misdemeanour, and the sentencing judge imposed 60 days.

Resurfaced audio has Paxton calling Uvalde shooting a plan by God

tags: politics
sources: @aaronparnas

Audio from a years-old podcast interview has recirculated in which Ken Paxton, the Republican nominee for Senate in Texas, described the Uvalde school shooting as a plan by God and said life is short. Paxton later called the shooting senseless in the same exchange. Twenty-one students and teachers were killed in the attack, one of the deadliest school shootings in US history. The clip is spreading again as Paxton runs for the Senate seat in the state where the shooting occurred.

Lula bans online betting by executive order days before Brazil election

tags: politics, health
sources: @groundnews

Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva signed an executive order banning online betting nationwide, reversing a framework that had licensed operators. The measure takes effect immediately but requires congressional approval within 120 days to remain law; betting sites can process withdrawals through October 5 before app stores and network providers must block them on October 6. Finance Minister Dario Durigan called online betting a serious public health issue, and the Finance Ministry estimates Brazilians spend about 60 billion reais ($11.57 billion) a year on it. The ban comes days before the October 4 presidential election in which Lula faces Senator Flavio Bolsonaro.

Sanders welfare ad featuring white recipient draws conservative backlash

tags: politics, media
sources: @groundnews

An advertisement from Arkansas Governor Sarah Huckabee Sanders promoting welfare work requirements, depicting a young white man named "Brad" playing video games and eating snacks while receiving assistance, drew criticism from conservative commentators. Longtime DeSantis aide Christina Pushaw wrote that they had found the one kind of ad allowed to feature white people, and former Trump lawyer Jenna Ellis warned against making young white men the enemy, a voting demographic she said Republicans need. The "End Wokeness" account, with 3.9 million followers, shared the ad alongside an earlier post mocking a Canadian assisted-dying advertisement.

Defence argues prosecutors failed to prove Lindsay Clancy killed her children

tags: legal
sources: @aaronparnas

At the first status conference since a mistrial was declared, defence attorney Kevin Reddington argued a motion to dismiss the charges against Lindsay Clancy, saying the Commonwealth did not prove she killed her children and that the case rests on speculation. He also argued the evidence did not establish criminal responsibility. Prosecutors opposed both points, and the judge will rule by November 2. The parties also argued over releasing sidebar transcripts and jury notes, including a Boston Globe request, and discussed a future trial date, with the defence saying it would not be ready before June of next year.

Administration weighs MLB game inside Grand Teton National Park

tags: climate, politics
sources: @groundnews

Major League Baseball has asked the Trump administration about staging a game in a national park, with a ballpark inside Wyoming's Grand Teton National Park under consideration and three possible sites explored, according to The Washington Post. The White House said MLB initiated the idea and that it is not a White House or administration priority. No site has been selected and the National Park Service has issued no permits. Grand Teton is the eighth most-visited US national park, and the earliest such a game could take place is 2028.

Army tests apps collecting soldiers' sleep and heart rate data

tags: surveillance, defence
sources: @oafnation_actual

The Army is testing applications and dashboards that could incorporate soldiers' sleep, heart rate variability, workout loads and diet information as part of its Holistic Health and Fitness Management System. Officials say they are still deciding what data should be collected, displayed and shared.

Destroyer returns to Pearl Harbor after 301-day Middle East deployment

tags: defence
sources: @oafnation_actual

Sailors aboard the USS Frank E. Petersen Jr. returned to Pearl Harbor after a 301-day deployment that included months in a Middle East combat zone. The commanding officer said the destroyer helped defend its strike group and other ships against more than 100 missile and drone attacks. The ship's longest stretch without a port visit was 106 days.

Former Boulder County deputy accused of firing on sheriff's headquarters

tags: legal, policing
sources: @oafnation_actual

Former Boulder County deputy Tyler Reilly was arrested after the sheriff's office said he threatened agency facilities and arrived at headquarters with an AR-15-style rifle, firing multiple rounds at the entrance while employees were inside. Investigators also suspect him of firing at police vehicles in Broomfield. Reilly resigned in 2024 in lieu of termination for cause. No injuries were reported and charges are pending.

Ohio appeals court upholds dismissal of gun charge over age limit

tags: legal
sources: @oafnation_actual

An Ohio appeals court upheld the dismissal of a felony concealed weapon charge against a man who was 19 at the time of the alleged offence. The court found the age restriction unconstitutional as applied to him.

Fort Carson staff sergeant arraigned over fake medical training scheme

tags: legal, defence
sources: @oafnation_actual

Army Staff Sgt. Christopher P. Allen has been arraigned on charges alleging he used fabricated "medical training" to order seven subordinate soldiers to undress, touched some inappropriately and directed soldiers to touch one another. He faces charges including abusive sexual contact, maltreatment and indecent exposure. He has not been convicted.

Military spouse sentenced to three years over conditions at Eglin home

tags: legal, defence
sources: @oafnation_actual

Devon Mae Witryk was sentenced to three years in federal prison after pleading guilty to felony child neglect, following the rescue of her child from conditions prosecutors described as absolutely deplorable at Eglin Air Force Base. The child's father was also court-martialed by the Air Force for his role.

Marine Corps updates incentives for extending overseas tours

tags: defence
sources: @oafnation_actual

The Marine Corps has revised the incentives offered to Marines who agree to remain at eligible overseas assignments for at least another 12 months. Options include $2,000 paid at $166.66 per month, up to 30 days of nonchargeable leave, or leave combined with government-funded travel to the continental United States. Updated location eligibility takes effect November 1.

Trump again appears to struggle to stay awake in Oval Office meeting

tags: politics
sources: @aaronparnas

The president appeared to struggle to stay awake during an Oval Office meeting concerning Iowa, the latest in a series of such incidents. In the same event he referred to Joe Biden as "sleepy Joe Biden," a nickname he has used for years. Explanations offered have ranged from long blinks to looking down at papers, while observers have pointed to late nights posting on Truth Social.

Team Trump account urges supporters to call off weddings over votes

tags: politics, media
sources: @aaronparnas

The official Team Trump account posted a video urging people to end engagements if their fiance did not vote for Trump, telling viewers to stop the wedding. The clip features Trump dancing.
